findings.finding: The change is safe because the identity line never enters context.items or the Responses input, so no checkpoint stores it and no later turn replays it. providers.ts builds the Gateway checkpoint from context.items plus the assistant text and puts the line only in the request array. responses.ts sends the line as the top-level instructions field, outside the input that trimCompacted keeps. A mutation in the lane proved the Gateway half. With the line added to the Gateway checkpoint, identity.test.ts failed only the test that a kimi reply never saves its identity into the checkpoint, with the diff 'Expected substring: not "running in the Glow app"', and the received checkpoint JSON held the system item. After the file was restored to the committed version, all 7 tests passed.
findings.none: The fact holds at the committed head.

findings.finding: Grep stops at the wire, so the request shape was read in the source. context.items never holds a system item, because the only other system textItem is the Kimi summary request in compaction/context.ts, and the summary comes back into the context as a user item. A Gateway reply therefore sends exactly one system message. The Kimi summary already sends a system message with array content through the same gatewayMessages mapping. DeepSeek replies send a system message for the first time. Whether every Gateway upstream accepts it, and whether Gateway chunks carry a top-level model, is unverified live. A chunk without a model only makes the log show answered=-.
findings.none: The fakes cover the request shape, and a live check needs a paid call that this change may not make. The next approved live check covers it.
